images.title: An algebra grid with two shapes
images.purpose: Shows the first practice grid, two squares and a circle make 27, two circles and a square make 21, with the values found.
images.composition: One two row grid in the centre with a small key of the two values underneath.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. A grid of 2 rows and 4 columns of equal square cells with thin dark outlines. Row 1: teal (#0072B2) square, teal square, amber (#E69F00) circle, then the number 27. Row 2: amber circle, amber circle, teal square, then the number 21. The sum column cells have a light grey (#6B7280) outline. Below the grid, centred, a key of two shapes side by side: one teal square with 11 written inside and one amber circle with 5 written inside. Exactly 8 grid cells, 3 squares and 3 circles in the grid, 1 square and 1 circle in the key.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each shape is one number: add the rows to find them.
images.description: Shows the first practice grid, two squares and a circle make 27, two circles and a square make 21, with the values found.
images.context: Rows added: 3 squares + 3 circles = 48, so square + circle = 16; square = 27 − 16 = 11, circle = 5.

image_decisions.why: The algebra grid is a visual object; one clean grid with its solved values shows the core move of the practice.
